checks.description: Project imports without an engine failure
Configured main scene runs
No candidate parse, script or resource loading errors
Live dashboard snapshots are available
Public dashboard shape and required numeric slots

New game | Advance opening dialogue | Show the five supplied opening lines in their original order, one per Enter, Space, or left-click press. The fifth confirmation closes the dialogue. | Auto-advance or advance several lines from one held key. | Current line and a continuation hint. | A fresh new game starts at line one.

Opening dialogue active | Attempt movement | Keep Gobot stationary until the last line closes, then enable movement. | Movement beneath the opening. | The dialogue remains the active interaction. | Closing the final line does not also move or interact with the world.

Exploring | Hold WASD or arrow keys | Move Gobot continuously; diagonal movement has the same total speed as cardinal movement. | Movement continuing after release. | Gobot visibly moves. | Movement keys work in each exploration region.

Exploring | Walk toward solid terrain or region boundaries | Trees, solid obstacles, and outer boundaries stop Gobot; designated entrances permit travel. | Walking through solids or becoming trapped on a transition. | Gobot stops at the obstacle. | Extend the map and its reachable paths as needed.

Any exploration region | Explore | Preserve the supplied Gobot and the starting forest's tile arrangement, paths, and clearings; keep a camera view useful for navigation while connecting new areas. | Replace the starter with an unrelated scene or genre. | Forest, robot, and navigable surroundings. | Additional regions may use a different layout.

Forest accessible | Explore | Provide a recognizable house exterior, its interior, and a deeper grove with player-accessible connecting entrances. | Require launching another scene from the editor. | Recognizable areas and entrance hints. | The house and grove entry prerequisites are QUEST-05 and PUZZLE-06.

At an unlocked entrance | Cross into another region or return | Place Gobot safely at the corresponding destination entrance; returning exits beside the corresponding exterior door. | Teleport into solids or immediately bounce indefinitely between entrances. | Visible arrival at the matching entrance. | The same route remains usable on later visits.

Near townsfolk or a world interactable | Press E or Space | Interact with the nearby object. At least four named townsfolk offer readable speaker-labelled dialogue; dialogue holds movement and can be continued with Enter, Space, or left click. | Trigger a distant object or move underneath dialogue. | Speaker, text, and interaction hint. | Escape closes optional conversations without awarding unfinished objectives; the opening is completed normally.

Explore the connected world | Travel between regions | Use the region and object landmarks in section 6.3.1; equivalent connected reachable locations are allowed. Every entrance to the deeper grove stays blocked until PUZZLE-06. | Bypass the three-pedestal gate through the forest entrance. | Consistent entrances and destination hints. | WORLD-02 controls safe return.

Before obtaining the Key | Speak to each of Warrior, Thief, Monk, and Wizard | Use the fixed names, positions, and dialogue in section 6.3. Each first conversation completes that townsfolk's objective and awards one Coin; later conversations do not award another. | Require house entry, grove entry, combat victory, or an unavailable consumable to earn the four Coins. | Objective instructions and completion feedback. | Any optional quest-specific object uses the corresponding quest-object observation kind.

One NPC objective completed, reward unclaimed | Claim that NPC reward | Award exactly one Coin. Four different completed objectives yield four Coins in total. | Award before that objective is completed. | Coin count and completed-objective progress toward four. | New game begins with zero Coins and zero completed/rewarded objectives.

NPC reward already claimed | Repeat conversation or revisit | Keep that reward claimed and leave Coin count unchanged. | Duplicate any Coin reward. | Completed dialogue or indication. | The claimed state survives reopening.

Fan the gatekeeper available | Request the exchange | Exchange exactly four Coins for one Key as one transaction; fewer than four Coins produce rejection with no deductions. | Partial payment or more than one Key from the exchange. | Trade result and updated inventory. | The exchange is one-time; repeat requests change nothing. New game has no Key.

At the locked house door | Interact with the door | With a Key, consume exactly one Key and unlock the house permanently; without it, keep the door locked without changing inventory. | Enter while locked or charge another Key after unlocking. | Locked rejection or visibly open door. | Unlock state survives returning and reopening.

Inside the unlocked house, chest unopened | Open the chest | Award exactly two Bombs and leave the chest visibly opened. | Duplicate Bombs on repeat interaction. | Chest-open feedback and Bomb count. | New game has zero Bombs; chest-open state survives reopening.

Inside house | Find the puzzle | Provide one Red, one Blue, and one Green wand and three matching, distinguishable pedestals. | Require inaccessible items beyond the blocked route. | Visible wand colors and matching pedestal colors. | New game has no held wands and no filled pedestals.

An uncollected wand is reachable | Pick up the wand | Add that color once to inventory and remove its world pickup. | Duplicate ownership on repeat interaction. | Pickup feedback and held color. | A placed wand does not respawn.

At a pedestal with a held wand | Choose a held color and confirm placement | A matching color leaves inventory and fills/lights that pedestal. Let the player choose a color explicitly so a mismatch can be attempted. | Fill other pedestals or consume another color. | Selected color, inventory update, and lit pedestal. | Cancelling color choice changes nothing.

At an empty pedestal | Confirm a wrong color or an unowned wand | Reject the placement without changing inventory or any pedestal; explain the mismatch or missing wand. | Auto-substitute a matching wand or consume the wrong color. | Visible rejection. | The player may choose again.

A pedestal is filled | Interact again | Keep its filled state without consuming another wand or issuing a reward. | Duplicate placement effects. | Already-filled indication. | Filled state persists after reopening.

Fewer than three pedestals filled, then all filled | Try the route; complete the remaining placements | Block entry to the deeper grove until all three are filled, then visibly open the route. The player travels through the open entrance. | Early passage or automatic teleport to the ending. | Blocked/open route feedback. | The open route remains open.

Ghost encounter accepted | Enter the offered battle | Use Baloo and Nutsy as the player party; the first encounter contains Bugcat enemies and the second Wolf enemies. The first contains three Bugcats and the second two Wolves, so group targeting is meaningful. | Require an editor launch or start Wolf before Bugcat victory. | Recognizable battlers and encounter identity. | Both party members start each attempt at full health. HP values are design choices.

Battle active | Choose actions as turns arrive | Show the current actor and take one committed action at a time, alternating through an understandable turn order including enemy turns. | Accept extra queued effects from repeated confirmation. | Actor/turn indication and action menu. | Once a player confirms an action, its animation and resulting enemy turns may complete without further input; waiting at a player menu does not advance the battle.

Living player actor has a turn | Choose an action, target, confirm, or cancel | Provide readable action descriptions, target selection/preview, and a separate confirmation; Escape cancels pending selection without spending the turn or changing HP. | Apply an effect on mere focus or selection. | Selected action and selected valid target(s). | Each action can be selected through visible clickable controls; target selection also has visible clickable targets.

Battle active | Damage or heal a combatant | Show current/max HP and a visible effect for the affected combatants. HP stays in [0,max]; HP zero is visibly downed. | Negative HP, over-healing, or unchanged display after an effect. | HP display and damage/heal/downed feedback. | Reported health matches the real battle state.

A combatant is downed | Choose a living target or advance turns | Exclude downed actors from acting and downed combatants from living-target selection. | Attack or heal a downed combatant as though living. | Downed/unavailable indication. | Victory/defeat follows the remaining living sides.

Baloo alive and acting | Confirm Bear Arms on a living enemy | Damage the selected living enemy. | Damage an ally or an unselected enemy. | Bear Arms label, description, and damage. | Damage amount is a design choice; no Bomb is required.

Nutsy alive and acting | Confirm First Aid on a living ally | Heal the selected living ally up to its maximum HP. | Heal an enemy, revive a downed ally, or exceed max HP. | First Aid label, description, and healing. | Healing a full-health living ally may have zero effect; it does not consume a Bomb.

Nutsy alive and acting | Confirm Nutsy's Arrow Storm action | Damage a selected living enemy without using a Bomb. | Leave Nutsy unable to attack when Bombs run out. | Action description and damage. | Damage and animation are design choices.

Baloo action menu | Inspect Bomb action | Show exactly one Bomb action with the supplied Bomb icon and label `Bomb xN`; at zero it remains visible and disabled. With Bombs and living targets it is enabled on Baloo's turn. | Duplicate or hide the action at zero. | Correct label/icon and enabled state. | It cannot be used by a downed/non-acting Baloo or with no living enemy.

Valid Bomb selected | Preview targets before confirmation | Highlight all and only living enemies as the pending targets. | Include allies or downed enemies; change HP/inventory during preview. | Visible group preview. | Cancellation removes the preview without an effect.

Valid Bomb confirmed | Resolve the effect | Apply exactly 35 damage once to every living enemy and to no ally/downed enemy; HP clamps at zero. | Repeat damage from repeated input or an animation callback. | Per-target damage/HP changes. | A target with less than 35 HP reaches zero; its displayed damage may still read 35.

Bomb effect successfully resolved | Finish the action | Consume exactly one Bomb after the successful effect; update all counts and save the new count. | Consume on selection/queueing or more than once per effect. | Bomb xN decreases once. | A Bomb ending the encounter still consumes once before victory is committed.

Cancellation, zero Bombs, invalid actor, rejected pending action, or no living target | Attempt/cancel Bomb use | Leave all HP and inventory unchanged. | Damage or consumption for an invalid/rejected action. | Cancellation or rejection feedback. | Remaining ordinary actions stay usable.

Enemy turn | Let the committed turn sequence resolve | Living enemies perform visible damaging actions against living party members. | Skip every enemy turn or use a downed enemy. | Enemy action and party HP change. | Enemy behavior and damage are design choices; a loss can be reached through normal poor choices.

All enemies downed | Finish the battle | Show victory, record this encounter once, and provide a visible continuation back to exploration near the ghost. | Leave combat inputs active under victory or immediately win the next encounter. | Victory and return control. | The next stage requires another player interaction.

Both party members downed | Finish the battle | Show defeat and a visible Retry control; leave this encounter unwon. | Record a victory or advance ghost progression. | Defeat, retry, and full-restart choices. | Gameplay inputs stop beneath the defeat screen.

Defeat screen | Choose Retry | Restart only that encounter with full party HP, reset enemy HP and transient turn/selection state, and retain committed inventory/progression including spent Bombs. | Refund used Bombs, clear earlier victories, or duplicate actors. | A clean attempt of the same encounter. | Full reset uses New Game/Restart instead.

Either encounter, even with zero Bombs | Use ordinary actions | Keep both encounters winnable with Bear Arms, First Aid, and Nutsy's attack. | Require a Bomb or another finite unavailable item to win. | Usable ordinary actions. | No timing challenge or real-time aiming is required to confirm turn-based actions.

Speak to townsfolk or ghost | Continue conversation | Use the required names and ordered dialogue in section 6.3.2/4. Warrior, Thief, Monk and Wizard each award only when the full first conversation completes. Fan moves to the second listed location after trading. | Award when Escape cancels an unfinished conversation. | Speaker-labelled lines and reward/trade feedback. | Runner, Smith and Sign remain optional.

Enter the house | Inspect pickups and pedestals | Provide the color/object arrangement in section 6.3.3, or equivalent reachable positions; any matching-color placement order is valid. | Enforce an unpublished placement order. | Distinct colors and lit pedestal feedback. | PUZZLE-01–06 define pickup and placement effects.

Baloo is alive and acting | Select and confirm Focus | Spend the current action to increase Baloo's next Bear Arms damage; show the pending boost and consume it on that next attack. | Damage an enemy immediately or consume a Bomb. | Focus label, description and boosted attack feedback. | Boost magnitude is a design choice; cancellation has no effect; retry clears it.

Grove reached normally | Meet the visible ghost | Provide dialogue connecting the ghost to the opening plea and offering the next required encounter. | Start an encounter before the player accepts. | Ghost dialogue and an encounter confirmation choice. | Cancelling leaves the current encounter unwon and allows another conversation.

Ghost progression revisited | Accept or cancel an encounter | Offer Bugcat first, Wolf only after Bugcat victory, and the final resolution only after both victories. | Duplicate an already won encounter or bypass an unfinished one. | Current stage in ghost dialogue. | Revisiting and cancellation preserve stage order.

Ghost reachable | Request final resolution | Only after all pedestals and both victories, resolve the opening plea and clearly announce that the grove is safe. | Announce success on an early visit, on defeat, or just on entering the grove. | Distinct ending message connected to the plea. | After the last victory the final ghost interaction is still required.

Exploration or non-outcome battle state | Press Escape when no cancellable selection/dialogue is active | Open pause with Resume, New Game/Restart, and Quit; resume returns to the same state. | Advance exploration or turns while paused. | Pause menu and labeled controls. | Pending selection/dialogue consumes Escape as cancellation first.

Ending or pause | Use lifecycle controls | Offer New Game/Restart and Quit. The ending blocks further gameplay while leaving these controls usable. | Continue movement or attacks underneath the ending. | Readable ending/pause options. | Quit closes normally after committed progress is saved.
Use the supplied principal artwork.

Exploration or combat | Obtain, spend, or place an inventory item | Coins, Key, Bombs, and held wands have consistent counts in the inventory HUD and relevant combat displays; counts never become negative. | Divergent exploration/combat inventory. | Counts update with the completed effect. | Opening inventory is all zero; internal storage architecture is unrestricted.

Inventory changed | Close normally and reopen in a fresh process | Restore committed Coin, Key, Bomb, and held-wand counts. | Refill a consumed Bomb or lose a collected item. | Restored inventory. | A completed effect is saved before normal closing can lose it.

Exploration progress changed | Close normally and reopen | Restore completed/claimed NPC objectives, trade, door, chest, pedestals, and grove-route states. | Respawn a claimed reward or undo a completed placement. | Restored world/objective state. | Counts and world flags stay consistent.

A region was entered | Close normally and reopen | Resume in that region at a safe corresponding entrance; exact walking position need not persist. The opening dialogue does not replay after it has been completed. | Spawn in a solid or require unlocking the same entrance again. | Recognizable restored region. | Closing during unfinished opening may restart the opening from line one.

Encounter active or completed; ending possibly reached | Close normally and reopen | Preserve won encounters and the ending. An unfinished battle resumes as a fresh attempt of that same encounter with full party HP, retaining already committed Bomb consumption. | Record an unfinished/lost encounter as won or refund used Bombs. | Restored encounter stage or ending. | Turn queues, transient selection, and animation positions need not persist.

Save absent or corrupt | Launch | Start a new game safely from the opening with zero inventory and no progression. | Use partial inconsistent progress or crash. | Opening dialogue; corrupt-save recovery may also display a notice. | Save-file location is the public TOOLCHAIN location.

Exploration, pause, defeat, or ending | Choose New Game/Restart | Return to opening line one; reset inventory, objectives/rewards, trade, door/chest, wands/pedestals, route, victories, ending, and pending battle state; replace old saved progress. | Restore old progress after restarting then reopening. | Fresh opening and reset state. | Ordinary retry is COMBAT-12, distinct from full restart.
